name: TRINIDAD
lead: Twin-island T&T sits 11 km off Venezuela — Trinidad was once attached to South America itself. It gave the world the steelpan, calypso, and one of Earth's wildest street parties. Underground lies a bubbling asphalt lake, and at dusk thousands of scarlet ibis glow red in the mangrove swamps.

sections.wows: Things that'll make you go wow

geo: Trinidad was once attached to South America — the Gulf of Paria between them is so shallow you could almost wade across. The Northern Range catches clouds and feeds lush rainforest; the south is flat and rich with oil.
Tobago, 30 km northeast, feels like a different world: coral reefs, quiet fishing villages, and jungle. Together the two islands cover 5,131 km² yet pack in extraordinary wildlife.
animals: Trinidad's national bird is the scarlet ibis — a flamingo-red wader that glows electric in the setting sun as thousands roost in Caroni Swamp. That vivid colour comes entirely from the shrimps they eat.
Tobago's bird is the cocrico, a noisy turkey-like forest creature that wakes everyone at dawn. Both appear on the coat of arms. The islands hold 470+ bird species — more than all of Europe.
culture: Carnival here is the template every other carnival copies. Before Lent, Port of Spain erupts in costumes, soca music, and J'ouvert — where revellers cover themselves in paint and mud before sunrise.
The steelpan was born in the 1930s when colonial rulers banned drumming. Young musicians hammered oil drums into tuned instruments — the only acoustic instrument invented in the 20th century.
history: Columbus landed in 1498 and named the island after three peaks he spotted. Spanish, French, and British colonisers followed. Enslaved Africans worked sugar plantations; after emancipation in 1838, indentured workers arrived from India.
Oil was struck in 1857. Independence came on 31 August 1962 with Dr. Eric Williams as first Prime Minister. The country became a republic in 1976 and is one of the Caribbean's wealthiest economies.
wows: Pitch Lake at La Brea holds 10 million tonnes of natural asphalt — Raleigh caulked his ships here in 1595.
Steelpan is the only acoustic instrument invented in the 20th century — the UN made 11 Aug World Steelpan Day.
Brian Lara of Trinidad scored 400 not out in 2004 — the highest individual Test innings ever played.
Trinidad rests on the South American shelf — geologically it IS South America, not a volcanic island.
Pitch Lake heals its own cracks; objects swallowed decades ago resurface later, perfectly preserved.
Over 470 bird species live here — more than the entire continent of Europe, in a country smaller than Devon.
Doubles — curried chickpeas in fried bara — were invented in the 1930s and millions eat them every morning.

myths.fact: It is two main islands plus 20+ smaller ones, 30 km apart and feeling totally different — one industrial and buzzing, one all reefs and rainforest.
Carnival belongs to Trinidadians. It grew from the resistance of enslaved Africans and is woven into national identity — most revellers are locals.
